confidence_notes: Music occupies PDF pages 3-17 (printed pages 3-17, 1:1 with PDF page number); PDF page 1 is the title page and page 2 is a blank verso, both zero-anchored; PDF page 18 is a blank pastedown (ghost bleed-through only), zero-anchored. This Jurgenson first edition has NO printed measure numbers anywhere and NO rehearsal numbers/boxed letters - every measure was derived by direct visual bar-counting (barline-by-barline) from 300dpi page renders, cross-checked with 2-4 overlapping crops per system where systems were dense or had mid-system meter/key changes. Systems per page are 5 throughout except page 12, which has 6 short systems ('Meno mosso'/Allegro reprise passage). Bars per system vary 1-4 depending on note density (dense 12/8 chordal writing = 3/system typically; slower dotted-half chords = 4/system; page 14 system5 is a genuine 1-bar system where the engraver broke the page mid-phrase during a fast 4/4 animando run). No repeat signs, D.C./D.S., or volta brackets found anywhere - the movement is through-composed. Meter changes between 12/8 and 4/4 occur several times (pp.5,7,9,10,11,16,17) and are noted in the log; these do not affect bar-counting since barlines were counted directly regardless of meter. programmatic staff-line/system-band detection (row-wise dark-pixel density) was attempted first (see detect_staves.py/detect_systems.py in the working dir) but proved unreliable on this aged scanned print (thin/broken staff lines, uneven ink, no vector data) - it either merged adjacent systems or split single systems into multiple bands. All yTopPct/yCenterPct values in this file are therefore VISUAL ESTIMATES (not programmatic), read off the same 300dpi crops used for bar-counting, each system's block cropped tightly enough to confirm its barlines; precision is targeted at ±0.02 but should be treated as lower-confidence than a programmatic staff-detection result. No anchors are flagged low_confidence individually because every system's bar count was re-verified via a dedicated zoomed crop (not just the initial overview pass) before being locked in; the two pages read only from top/bottom half overviews without a further dedicated per-system recheck are pages 4 and 5, where bar counts were unambiguous (clean 3-bar systems, no boundary ambiguity) - noted for transparency. The final system (p.17, 'Meno mosso') ends on a thick double barline confirming the end of the piece; a small mark above the final chord may be a fermata but the scan resolution does not confirm this definitively - flagged as a caveat, not a low_confidence anchor since it does not affect measure count. Total: 76 anchors over 15 pages, continuity chain (each system's start = previous start + previous system's bar count) closes at measure 240 (piece runs m1-m240); there is no independent MusicXML or printed-number cross-check available for this source (per task scope), so validation is internal-chain-only as instructed.
